newsitem.title: UK: BT, Cable & Wireless off on competition fears.
newsitem.headline: BT, Cable & Wireless off on competition fears.

text.p: Shares in British Telecoms and Cable & Wireless edged lower on Thursday after a Financial Times report saying the UK is preparing to open its international telecoms market fully to competition.
Cable & Wireless shares were off 4-1/2p at 473-1/2p and BT was down 1/2p at 358-1/2p amid fears that the companies could see a significant fall in overseas telecoms revenues.
The FT reported today that the UK is set to award licences to all 46 companies seeking to compete with BT and C&W in offering rival services.
The move is designed to increase inward investment and may also defuse opposition to the proposed $20 billion merger of BT and MCI Communications.
But traders said expectations of growing competition had already been discounted in the share prices of the UK's biggest telecoms groups.

"We've known since July that a large number would apply for licences and a large number would be granted, so it's already in the prices," said James Golob, telecoms analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts said the extent to which revenues will suffer as a result of the loss of market share is hard to predict.
"The exact impact on earnings will depend on how the new operators comply with the principle of proportional return," Golob said.
"But Mercury will suffer more than BT because international traffic makes up a much higher proportion of total traffic for Mercury and contributes a higher proportion of total profits."
